title: F172 - Lesson 10: Gene Therapy Clinical Trials & Task 2 Research (ANT-130)
courseName: OCR Level 3 Cambridge Advanced National (AAQ) in Human Biology - Unit F172: Genetics
focus: Gene Therapy Clinical Trials & Task 2 Research: ANT-130 (AMT-130) Case Study, Biomarkers, and OCR Genetics NEA Marking Criteria
deliverable: OCR AAQ Level 3 Human Biology (Unit F172: Genetics) Lesson 10 presentation focusing on clinical trial phases (I-III), uniQure ANT-130 (AMT-130) AAV5-miRNA striatal microinfusion for Huntington's disease, CSF biomarker analysis (mHTT and NfL), functional metrics (cUHDRS, TMS), genetic counselling ethics, and comprehensive alignment to OCR Genetics NEA Task 2 marking rubrics (Pass P5/P7/P8, Merit M3/M4/M5, Distinction D3/D4/D5).

objectives.knowledge: Explain clinical trial architecture (Phases I–III) and the molecular mechanism of ANT-130 (AAV5-miRNA targeting HTT mRNA via RNAi).
objectives.application: Interpret primary clinical trial data: dose-dependent CSF mHTT reduction, transient vs chronic Neurofilament Light (NfL) dynamics, and cUHDRS functional deceleration.
objectives.evaluation: Evaluate trial methodology (sham controls, small cohorts, irreversible intracranial surgery) and align coursework to Genetics NEA Task 2 Distinction criteria.

terminology.def: An investigational AAV5-miRNA gene therapy delivering microRNA directly into the caudate and putamen to silence toxic mutant huntingtin (mHTT) via RNA interference.
A sensitive biomarker of active neuroaxonal damage; initial post-operative spike followed by long-term decline below baseline indicates neuroprotection.
A multidimensional clinical rating score combining total motor score, total functional capacity, and cognitive measures to assess Huntington's disease progression.
OCR AAQ Level 3 coursework evaluating gene therapies against Pass (P5, P7, P8), Merit (M3, M4, M5), and Distinction (D3, D4, D5) criteria.

slides.title: F172 Lesson 10: Gene Therapy Clinical Trials & Task 2 (ANT-130)
slides.subtitle: OCR AAQ Level 3 Human Biology · Unit F172: Genetics (Matt)
keyTakeaways: Core focus on ANT-130 / AMT-130 clinical trial architecture and NEA Task 2 criteria.
Detailed analysis of biomarker curves, sham surgical controls, and evaluative grading.

slides.title: Clinical Trial Architecture: From Bench to Bedside
slides.subtitle: Phases I, II, and III investigational design and regulatory thresholds
keyTakeaways: Phase I assesses safety, dose escalation, and toxicity in small cohorts (N=10-30).
Phase II demonstrates biological activity, target engagement, and surrogate biomarkers (N=30-100).
Phase III conducts multi-centre randomized controlled trials for definitive efficacy.

slides.title: Huntington's Disease: Pathology & Genetic Architecture
slides.subtitle: Autosomal dominant CAG expansion, mHTT aggregation, and striatal degeneration
keyTakeaways: CAG trinucleotide repeat expansion (>36 repeats) in HTT gene exon 1 on chromosome 4.
Misfolded toxic mutant huntingtin (mHTT) protein triggers medium spiny neuron apoptosis.
Leads to progressive motor chorea, cognitive executive decline, and psychiatric symptoms.

slides.title: ANT-130 (AMT-130) Molecular Mechanism of Action
slides.subtitle: AAV5 vector capsid, microRNA expression, and RNAi-mediated HTT knockdown
keyTakeaways: Recombinant AAV5 carries artificial microRNA engineered to target human HTT transcripts.
Administered via bilateral stereotactic Convection-Enhanced Delivery into striatal nuclei.
miRNA loads into RISC complex, cleaving HTT mRNA and reducing toxic mHTT protein levels.

slides.title: ANT-130 Clinical Trial Design & Control Methodology
slides.subtitle: Phase I/II multi-centre trial (NCT04120493) and sham surgical control
keyTakeaways: Multi-centre randomized trial evaluating low-dose, high-dose, and imitation surgical controls.
Sham surgery involves partial burr holes without dural penetration to control for placebo effect.
Longitudinal follow-up tracks patients across 24, 36, and up to 60 months post-infusion.

slides.title: Objective Biomarker Findings: mHTT & Neurofilament Light (NfL)
slides.subtitle: CSF target knockdown and neuroaxonal preservation trajectories
keyTakeaways: High-dose ANT-130 demonstrated sustained, dose-dependent CSF mHTT reduction.
CSF NfL exhibits transient acute elevation from surgical trauma, followed by drop below baseline.
Long-term NfL reduction proves deceleration in underlying neuronal degeneration.

slides.title: Clinical Functional Efficacy: cUHDRS & Total Motor Score
slides.subtitle: Deceleration of clinical disease progression compared to natural history
keyTakeaways: High-dose cohort showed significant preservation on composite UHDRS (cUHDRS) at 24-36 months.
Total Motor Score (TMS) demonstrated marked slowing of chorea and motor deterioration.
Distinguishes between statistical p-value significance and meaningful clinical quality of life.

slides.title: Role of Genetic Counselling & Ethical Considerations
slides.subtitle: Predictive presymptomatic testing, autosomal dominance, and patient autonomy
keyTakeaways: 50% inheritance risk requires pre-test counselling on psychological and family implications.
'The Right Not to Know' protects autonomy for asymptomatic individuals in affected pedigrees.
Counsellors manage expectations: ANT-130 stabilizes disease but cannot reverse lost brain tissue.

slides.title: Critical Evaluation: Strengths vs Structural Limitations
slides.subtitle: Merit analytical depth vs Distinction critical evaluation
keyTakeaways: Strengths (Merit): Direct CSF biomarkers, CED delivery bypassing BBB, multi-year monitoring.
Limitations (Distinction): Small sample size (N<30), sham control unblinding after 12 months, non-selective wild-type HTT knockdown, irreversible intracranial surgery.

slides.title: OCR AAQ Unit F172 Genetics NEA Task 2 Marking Rubric
slides.subtitle: Grading criteria breakdown across Pass, Merit, and Distinction tiers
keyTakeaways: Pass (P5, P7, P8): Accurate disorder description, AAV5 delivery route, and RNAi mechanism.
Merit (M3, M4, M5): Trial methodology critique, sham control evaluation, and biomarker interpretation.
Distinction (D3, D4, D5): Evaluative synthesis, sample size critique, irreversible surgical risk analysis, and Harvard referencing.
